title: Detect list truncation by querying limit+1 rows, then slicing
answers: How do I report that a capped setup context list was truncated?
Why does the target surface query use TARGET_SURFACE_MAX_LIBS + 1?
body:
Capped lists in setup_context.py expose a `*_truncated` boolean rather than making agents guess from row count (exactly cap rows is ambiguous).
Pattern in _compute_target_surface: query `limit = MAX + 1`, build libs from `rows[:MAX]`, set `libs_truncated = len(rows) > MAX`. Same as sdk_profile.libs_truncated.
Tests need both an at-cap case (false) and an above-cap case (true); see test_libs_are_truncated_only_above_the_cap, which catches `>` vs `>=` mistakes.
The skill (setup-decisions.md) must read the flag, not the row count; existing flags: sdk_profile.libs_truncated, sdk_profile.libs_on_any_event_truncated, shared_metrics.metric_event_match_truncated.
says: Capped lists expose truncated flag instead of leaving cap status ambiguous
Query one more than the maximum row count to reliably detect truncation
Use truncated boolean to signal when list exceeds the cap limit
Row count alone cannot distinguish at-cap from above-cap results
Setup context surface lists report whether they were truncated or complete
search: Capped lists in setup_context.py expose a *_truncated boolean flag rather than making agents infer truncation from row count. Query `limit = MAX + 1`, slice rows to `rows[:MAX]` for the list, and set `truncated = len(rows) > MAX` (not >=, which is a common pitfall). The pattern appears in _compute_target_surface and applies to existing flags: sdk_profile.libs_truncated, sdk_profile.libs_on_any_event_truncated, and shared_metrics.metric_event_match_truncated. Tests in test_setup_context.py must cover both the at-cap case (false) and above-cap case (true) to catch > vs >= bugs. Skills and downstream code must read the flag, not infer from row count. Applies to any capped list in setup_context.py where distinguishing full results from truncated results matters.
